clusters.title: A 'no (bolt) holes in the web / flanges / short leg / elsewhere' is read as 'the whole member is welded', or a lazy skip runs across the negation and counts web lines
clusters.root_cause: reader.js tensionCommon line 1612 `if (/no\s+bolt\s+holes/i.test(t)) welded = true;` fires on any 'no bolt holes', with no check of what follows ('in the web', 'in the flanges', 'elsewhere', 'the short leg has ...') and even after a bolt size and hole counts were read. findHoles line ~1205-1206 (the weldedWord regex) has the same unscoped `no\s+bolt\s+holes|...|no\s+holes\b`. The welded test at line 1610 also ignores H.cutFlange, H.lines and H.across, so 'no holes in the web' plus '4 holes in the flanges' becomes welded (tcap-08). Welded mode skips every hole count, so only yielding is computed (702 printed where 596.2 is right). findHoles line 1147 (web lines) and its 'through ... lines of' twins use the lazy skip `(?:\S+\s+){0,5}?`, which crosses ', no ' and reads the negated 'bolts/holes through the web' as web lines (tcap-09/10/11). H.web then wins over H.noWeb. pipeline.js line 3347-3352 (the 'mentions bolts or holes' guard) is switched off by its own exclusion `\bno\s+(?:bolt\s+)?holes?\b`. I checked this on the branch: the same text without 'no bolt holes in the web' prints 596.2.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js only, plus one small pipeline hunk. (1) findHoles weldedWord regex (~1205): `no\s+bolt\s+holes` and `no\s+holes\b` count as welded only when NOT scoped. Add a negative lookahead for `\s+(?:are\s+|is\s+)?(?:in|through|on|at)\s+(?:the\s+|its\s+|either\s+|each\s+|any\s+)?(?:web|stem|flanges?|(?:short|long|outstanding|other)?\s*legs?)` and `\s+elsewhere`. Check 'X has no bolt holes' with a slice test on the text before the match (ES5, no lookbehind). (2) tensionCommon line 1612: use the same scoped test, and add `&& !F.bolt && !H.perFlange && !H.cutFlange && !H.web && !H.lines && !H.perLine && !H.across && !H.inSection && !H.forBolt`. Line 1610: add the same count slots. (3) noWeb/noFlange regexes: make the article optional ('no bolt holes in web'), so the scoped phrase still sets web_holes = 0. (4) Line 1147 and its twins: the token skip may not cross a comma, a semicolon or a negation: `(?:(?!(?:no|not|none|without)\b)[^\s,;]+\s+){0,5}?`. If H.web and H.noWeb are both set, raise a count_web ask (kind 'need'), never a silent override. (5) pipeline.js 3349: the exclusion keeps only an unscoped 'no holes'. ANSWER where the reading is single: tcap-01/02/03/05/07 give 596.2 / 471.1 / 152.3, tcap-06 gives 168.2 (Case 8), tcap-08/09 give 596.2, tcap-04 gives U = 0.90. ASK: tcap-10 then falls to the '2 lines in the flanges' halving rule (cluster tension-geometry-multiplier: 1 or 2 per flange), and tcap-11 (no flange word) asks holes_count. MUST NOT CHANGE: a bare 'no bolt holes' / 'there are no holes' / 'welded' / 'all connections are welded' stays welded and yielding only. Also unchanged: '(there are no bolts in the web)' with flange counts (noWeb), her May 2024 Q8 'four lines ... through its flanges' (2 per flange), and gross-section-yielding mode.

clusters.title: A tension count's multiplier or a size's kind is chosen silently: two angles, both legs, bolts per flange vs holes, each side of the web, halved lines, hole diameter vs bolt diameter
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findHoles / tensionCommon / findBolt take one reading of a geometry word without a second check. (a) tensionCommon lines 1585 and 1602: angles = 2 only for a 2L name or the adjacent `(double|pair of|two) angles`. 'two L4x4x1/2 angles' (the shape name in between) drops the count (tcap-12/13: half the strength). (b) Nothing reads 'both legs' / 'each leg'. findHoles yields H.lines = 1, so line ~1661 sets holes_across = 1, and the connection rule at ~1713 (`memberIsAngle && (H.locLeg || F.bolt ...)`) gives Case 8 'one leg' (tcap-14/15/16). (c) findHoles line ~1091 `(WN) ... (holes?|bolts?) (in|across|through) (each|every|both) flanges?` takes a BOLT count per flange as holes across, even when 'N bolts per line' is in the text (6 bolts/3 per line = 2 lines; tcap-17). (d) The each-side-of-the-web doubling (~1070-1075) runs only when no per-flange count was read, and cgApply had already set perFlange = 1 from the same phrase (tcap-18). (e) tensionCommon 1641-1644 halves cutFlange 'N lines of bolts in/through the flanges' to N/2 per flange (confidence medium) without an ask. That is right for her Q8 'four lines', but '2 lines ... in the flanges' has two readings (tsel-13). (f) findBolt line 1228 (pattern 4) returns kind 'bolt' even when its noun is 'holes' ('holes are 15/16 in. in diameter'), so the existing bolt_or_hole path never runs and hole + 1/8 is applied to a hole (tcap-22/23).
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js only. (a) Lines 1585/1602: also accept `\b(?:two|2|double|pair\s+of)\s+(?:L\s?\d[\w\/.\s-]{0,14}?\s+)?angles?\b` when exactly one L name is in the text: ANSWER (angles = 2). (b) For an angle with 'through/in both legs' or 'each leg': U = 1.0 (Case 1, every element connected, her case). Set holes_across = 2 x lines only when a per-leg line count is read ('one line in each leg'); otherwise ASK holes_across (kind 'need'). Never Case 8. tcap-14 gives 140.2, tcap-15 gives U = 1.0, tcap-16 gives An = 2.875. (c) Line ~1091: if the noun is 'bolts' and a per-line count exists, holes per flange = N / perLine when it divides evenly (ANSWER 2 for 6/3). Otherwise ASK count_perFlange ('need'). A bolt count is never holes. (d) Each-side doubling: also apply it when the per-flange count came from the same 'on each side of the web' clause (ANSWER 2 per flange). If another per-flange number was typed, use the existing conflict ask. (e) Line 1641: keep the halving for N >= 4 (her Q8). N = 2 'lines in/through the flanges' raises a count_perFlange question naming both readings. The existing count_ mechanism (pipeline markReaderStops) empties the box and asks. (f) findBolt line 1228: kind = /hole/i.test(noun) ? 'hole' : 'bolt'. The existing bolt_or_hole / MISSING path then asks. Never add 1/8 to a hole. MUST NOT CHANGE: 2L names, 'double angles', HW 3-23 'one each side of the web' (2 per flange), 'N holes per flange', one-leg angles (Case 8, U from her table), 'four lines ... through its flanges' = 2 per flange.

clusters.title: The bolt words are there but no bolt size or hole count is read (glued '3/4inbolts', '2perflange', 'bolted 3/4in'): the asks are non-blocking, so only yielding is computed
clusters.root_cause: reader.js tensionCommon line 1625 (B.ask 'bolt_dia') and lines 1649/1673 (B.ask 'holes_count') are raised with no kind, so they default to kind 'value'. pipeline.js markReaderStops (2997-3015) blocks only 'stop' and 'need', so the engine runs with empty hole boxes as 'no holes' (702 / 318.6 printed). The safety guard in pipeline.js 3346-3352 covers only tension_capacity/tension_net_area, not tension_select (tsel-10, 12). It tests `\b(?:bolt(?:s|ed)?|holes?)\b`, and there is no word boundary inside the glued 'inbolts' / '2holes' / '3bolts' (tcap-19, tsel-11). The trigger is pipeline.js normalizeTyped line 1864: the glued-unit splitter refuses 'in' followed by a letter ('3/4inbolts'). findHoles line 1117 needs \s+ before 'per' and a \b(holes?|bolts?)\b in the text ('bolted' does not count).
clusters.fix_plan: (1) reader.js tensionCommon 1625, 1649/1650, 1673: when the member is not welded and the text contains bolt|hole|rivet as a SUBSTRING (not \b, so glued words count), raise these asks with kind 'need'. The gate then asks ONE question instead of printing yielding only. (2) pipeline.js 3347: extend the guard regex to tension_select and use the substring test (one-line hunk). (3) Coverage only, after (1)-(2) are in: normalizeTyped 1864 also splits `(\d)(in)(?=bolts?|holes?|dia)`, and `(\d)(per|holes?|bolts?|lines?)\b` becomes 'N per'. These are splits only and change no reading. ANSWER where the reader then reads the size and counts. ASK (need) otherwise. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'select lightest w8 welded' (no bolt word, no ask), 'no holes' / welded members, plates and angles whose counts are read, selections where the hole counts are read.

clusters.title: Only one of D / L is read and the other, named in the words (D=, L=, dead, live, 'twice the dead load', 'each'), is silently taken as 0
clusters.root_cause: reader.js fillAxialLoads lines 1457-1468: `if (d) B.set('D'...); if (l) B.set('L'...)` sets whichever kind was read and never asks for the other, although the text names it. The frozen engine's loadFromArgs then uses 0 (1.4D governs, Pu = 70 / 160 / 240 printed). FILL.loads_takedown line 2497 asks only when BOTH floor loads are missing (`if (!d && !l)`), so 'live load twice the dead load' becomes 0 (csel-06). The numbers are lost upstream in findLoads: the bare 'D = 50 k' rule (line 256-264) needs a load unit right after EACH number ('D=50 L=100 kips', 'D = 30, L = 60 kips', 'L=150', 'D = L = 75 kips'). The kind-named rule at 312 needs a unit ('dead 100 live 150 kips'). No rule reads 'twice / N times the dead load', 'L = 2D' or 'dead and live loads are each 50 kips'. Unitless numbers never reach the unused-number gate either. I checked this on the branch: 'D=50k L=100 kips' prints W8X18 (right).
clusters.fix_plan: (1) Smallest safe guard, reader.js fillAxialLoads after line 1466: if exactly one of d/l was read and the text names the other kind, raise B.ask('load_L' or 'load_D', 'Your question names a live (dead) load but the page did not read its number. Type L (D) in kips.', ['L'] or ['D'], null, 'need'). Dead: `\b(?:P\s?_?)?D(?:L)?\s*=|\bdead\b`. Live: `\b(?:P\s?_?)?L(?:L)?\s*=(?![\d.\s\/]*(?:ft|feet|foot|in\b|'))|\blive\b`. Skip the ask when the words say the load is absent ('no live load', 'live load is zero', 'dead load only'). (2) The same in FILL.loads_takedown line 2497 for floor_D_psf / floor_L_psf (kind 'need'). (3) Coverage only where unambiguous, in findLoads: a bare pair sharing ONE trailing unit ('D=50 L=100 kips', 'D = 30, L = 60 kips': joined by space, comma or 'and', unit after the last) reads both in that unit. 'D = L = 75 kips' reads both as 75. 'dead and live loads are each 50 kips' reads both as 50. 'live load is twice / N times the dead load' gives L = N x D only when D was read with a unit. Anything else stays MISSING and goes to the ask, never 0. MUST NOT CHANGE: dead-load-only questions with no live word (XA-19, DS-21), 'L = 25 ft' (a length), L-shape names (L4x4), PD/PL symbols, a given factored Pu, takedowns that read both floor loads.

clusters.title: A load number is bound to the wrong kind or coefficient: a gap that crosses another load label, a number-first rule that binds across a label, an expression's first coefficient, a D/L slash pair read as a fraction, a substring test that hides a snow load, 'factored loads D=' not seen as factored
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findLoads. (a) Line 236, the symbol form `... (?:=|:)\s*(N)(?:\s*-?\s*(UNITS)|(?![A-Za-z0-9]))`: the unitless branch accepts '1.2' in 'Pu = 1.2(100) + 1.6(150)' because '(' is not alphanumeric, so Pu = 1.2 kips is a given factored load ('adequate for Pu = 1.2'). (b) Line 258 / 312: in 'D/L = 200/300 kips' and 'dead/live = 80/50 psf' the '/' is a boundary, so only 'L = 200/300' / 'live = 80/50' match. N's fraction branch (line 87) turns them into 0.667 / 1.6, and D is lost. (c) The word-form gap at line 268 `[^0-9.;=]{0,28}?` runs from 'live load' across ' is twice the dead load of ' (csel-07) and takes the dead load's number as the live load. (d) The number-first rule at line 292 binds '80 psf live' across the label boundary in 'dead 80 psf live 100 psf'. Rule 312 then skips 'dead 80 psf' and 'live 100 psf' as overlaps, so D is missing and L = 80 (csel-08/09). The unused '100 psf' is then hidden across the chain by pipeline.js computeUnused 2463 / unusedOf 2619. (e) Rule 292 accepts only dead|live, so '50 k snow' is not read. readChunk's safety net (line ~2611, occ substring test) finds '50 k' inside '150 k live', so the number is not listed as unplaced (csel-24). (f) loadBasis line 1426 givenFactored misses 'factored loads D=200k L=300k' (a symbol stands between 'loads' and '='), so D and L are refactored (720 for 500; csel-11).
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js only. (a) Line 236: reject the unitless branch when the number is followed by `\s*[(*x+]` or a second number. When 'Pu =' / 'P =' is followed by an arithmetic expression, raise B.ask('pu_formula', 'Your question writes the load as a formula: work it out and type Pu in kips.', ['Pu'], null, 'need'). ASK, no number in the message. (b) Lines 258/312: a slash pair of two symbols or two kinds ('D/L', 'dead/live') followed by a slash pair of two numbers is read in order (D = a, L = b, with the shared unit): ANSWER, because the order is unambiguous. Any other slash after a load symbol does not use the fraction branch; it stays MISSING and goes to the cluster load-pair-half-missing ask. (c) Line 268 gap: it may not cross another load-kind word or a load symbol with '=' or 'if': `(?:(?!\b(?:dead|live|snow|wind|rain|roof)\b|\b[DLSWPw]{1,2}\s*=|\bif\b)[^0-9.;=]){0,28}?`. The live load is then not read and the half-missing ask follows. (d) Line 292: skip a match whose number is directly preceded by a kind word (`(dead|live|snow|wind)\s*(?:=|:)?\s*$` on the slice before). Rule 312 then reads 'dead 80 psf' and 'live 100 psf': ANSWER 921.6 / 264. (e) Rule 292: add snow, so loads_combinations reads S = 50 (ANSWER 385 by the page's 7-combination form). In readChunk occ(): a match counts only when the character before it is not a digit or '.', so a missed load stays unplaced and blocking. (f) loadBasis: also `factored\s+loads?\s*,?\s*(?:[A-Za-z]{1,3}\s*=)` and '(factored)' / 'these are factored loads' give 'factored'. The existing loads_basis ask follows (ASK, not a silent sum). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'PD = 115 k', 'Pu = 800 kips', '100 k dead + 150 k live', the 'dead + live = 120 psf is a sum' guard, '3/4 in' fractions in bolt sizes, the framing-weight rule of C-28.

clusters.title: A question with no blank asks for nominal / bare Pn / one limit state / ASD / excess / percent / L/r / KL / Euler critical stress / KL/r about x, and the form's governing phi Pn (or K, Pcr) stays a clean ANSWER
clusters.root_cause: pipeline.js prose path. The words that change the quantity live only on the blank path, in wordId line 922 (`excess|extra|percent|nominal|allowable|asd|omega ...`) and lines 925-941 (yield -> phipn_y, rupture -> phipn_r). The sentence path never applies them. (1) asksInProse line 1002 needs an asking verb, or 2+ symbols with no digit, so 'nominal yield strength', 'design strength for yielding?', 'gross yielding?', 'phi Pn for rupture', 'L/r?' and '(d) rupture strength' ask nothing. (2) ASK_WORDS 975-999 has no bare 'Pn'/'nominal' entry. The phipn entry (989) matches 'tensile strength' inside 'nominal tensile strength' and becomes the form's own result. There is no 'rupture strength' / 'yielding strength' entry. The fe entry (998) has no /i flag and no 'euler critical stress'. The klr entry (978) ignores 'about the x axis', and there is no prose 'KL'. (3) askedInWords 1007-1035 has no qualifier test. (4) The limit-state block in signaturePass 1334-1343 already detects 'for yielding' / 'rupture strength' (ls = 'y' / 'r'), but only RENAMES an existing phipn ask, and here there is none. (5) writeBlock line 3841: allProse never demotes the form's ANSWER while STRENGTH_ASK (1038) matches 'strength' / 'capacity'. I confirmed on the branch that tcap-31 parts (c) and (d) still print the governing 596.2 as ANSWER.
clusters.fix_plan: Put a small helper in a NEW file (or wordsx.js), called at the end of askedInWords, with one-line hunks in signaturePass and writeBlock. (1) A part's LAST sentence with no digit that ends in '?' or is a bare noun phrase naming a known quantity counts as asking. (2) Apply wordId's qualifier list to the asking sentence. 'allowable|ASD|omega' gives a not-in-tool sentence (one sentence, no number: her class is LRFD), so tsel-29 / ccap-283 STOP. 'excess|extra|additional|margin|percent|utiliz|remaining|reserve' pushes an UNKNOWN ask (part.unknownBlanks = the phrase). The existing 'CHECK YOUR BLANK' line then stands under the ANSWER (tsel-23/24/25: not clean, no new number). (3) 'nominal' or a bare 'Pn' (no phi) gives id pn / pn_y / pn_r with the limit-state words. SIG_NOMINAL then prints column Pn = phi Pn / 0.9 (ccap-269/270: 974.4, unambiguous) and tension Pn_y = yielding/0.9, Pn_r = rupture/0.75 (tsel-27: 332.3; tcap-26: 485.5... only if Pn_y/Pn_r come from her phis). A tension 'Pn' with no limit state (two phis) is an UNKNOWN ask, so a CHECK warning shows (tcap-24/25, tsel-26). Exclude 'nominal' before the phipn ASK_WORDS match. (4) signaturePass 1342: when ls is set and no phipn/pn ask exists on a tension part, push a prose ask phipn_y / phipn_r (pn_y / pn_r with 'nominal'). This ANSWERs the form's own yielding/rupture value (702, 437, 135.9, 318.6): unambiguous by her method. (5) writeBlock 3841: allProse also demotes the form's ANSWER to ALSO FOUND when every prose ask is one of {phipn_y, phipn_r, pn, pn_y, pn_r, fe, klrx, klry, kl}, even when STRENGTH_ASK matches. (6) ASK_WORDS: fe gets /i and 'Euler (critical|buckling) stress' (ANSWER Fe 20.28). 'KL/r about the x|strong|major axis' maps to klrx, and y|weak|minor to klry (ANSWER 55.56). 'effective length KL' / a final 'KL' maps to 'kl' (existing id; only with one length: ANSWER 16 ft). 'L/r?' is caught by (1) (ANSWER 96.8). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'Determine the design tensile strength. Report An, U and Ae' (the strength stays ANSWER), her review 'Find: Euler Pcr, the AISC phi Pn' (never flagged), 'for yielding and rupture' (no single limit state), the whole blank path, and 'Design strength for yielding of the gross section' (already right). Run harness/regress.sh and classify every changed line.

clusters.title: A REQUIRED area (Ag required, min Ag, required Ae / net area) is answered with the chosen shape's Ag, or with the required-Ag headline when Ae was asked
clusters.root_cause: pipeline.js. In wordId, the in2 symbol shortcut at line 936 (`/ ag /` -> 'ag') runs BEFORE the required/minimum/min/needed guard at line 954. 'Ag required = ____ in2' becomes id 'ag', and SIG_VALUE.ag (/^Ag$/ first) returns the selected W8X18's 5.26 (tsel-20). askedInWords line 1016 SKIPS ag/an/ae whenever 'required|minimum|needed|necessary' is in the sentence. So 'required Ae?' and 'required net area' add no ask and the form's 'Required gross area: Ag' headline stays clean (tsel-18/19). The list has no 'min', so 'min Ag?' adds a plain 'ag' ask that returns the shape's Ag (tsel-21). tsel-09: the frozen finder routes 'required gross area' with no tension word to loads_factored, and no amendRoute rule (760-787) corrects it. Its live load ('3 times the dead load') is also unread (load-pair-half-missing). The engine already holds Ag_required (tension_select, tension_required_area) and Ae_required (tension_required_area).
clusters.fix_plan: pipeline.js, small hunks. (1) wordId: move the `/ required | minimum | min | needed | req d /` test above the in2 shortcuts (935-936). Map 'required/min Ag' to a new id 'agreq' (SIG_VALUE [/^Ag_required$/]) and 'required Ae' to 'aereq' ([/^Ae_required$/]). Add both to SIG_LABEL. In sigGives, tension_required_area gives agreq (main) and aereq (also), and tension_select gives agreq (also). (2) askedInWords 1016: instead of skipping, push agreq / aereq. 'required net area An' has no single value (it needs U and the hole layout), so push an UNKNOWN ask and the CHECK warning shows. (3) tsel-09: one amendRoute rule. 'required (gross|effective) area' / 'Ag required' with loads in kips and no column/beam/moment word moves to tension_required_area. Its unread live load then gets the load-pair ask. ANSWER: required Ag = Pu/(0.9 Fy) and required Ae = Pu/(0.75 Fu) (D2a/D2b, her method: tsel-20/21 4.889, tsel-19 3.938, tsel-18 Ae 3.034). ASK/CHECK: required An. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'Ag = ____' of a capacity question (the shape's own Ag), 'Show Ag required and the L/r check' extra lines, beams' required Zx (lookup_by_property rule 2), the C-48 'a36 is not a required Zx' rule.

clusters.title: 'max / max. / maximum LL / max dead / maximum total service load' asked on a capacity question: the route stays capacity and the phi Pn line is the clean ANSWER
clusters.root_cause: The frozen finder-data.js T-maxl signals ('max live', 'maximum live', 'maximum service live') miss 'max service live' (tsel-30, tcap-21, ccap-307), 'max. live' (tsel-31) and 'maximum LL' (tsel-32). reader.js ASKDEFS max_load (line ~513) needs 'maximum|largest|how much live load', so no capacity>loads_max_service chain is built. No form solves for the maximum DEAD load or D + L (tsel-33/34/35). pipeline.js amendRoute (760-787) has no rule for these, askedInWords has no live-load ask, and STRENGTH_ASK (1038) matches 'maximum service dead load' / 'strength'. The capacity line therefore stays the ANSWER. In tcap-21 / ccap-307 the live load is also stolen from 'D = 100k' / 'dead load = 100 kips' (the word-form gap of cluster load-number-misbound). I checked this on the branch: 'find maximum live load' already chains and prints 125.76.
clusters.fix_plan: (1) A spelling pre-pass before the finder: pipeline normalizeTyped (one line), or expand.js if it runs first. `\bmax\.?(?=\s+(?:service\s+|unfactored\s+)?(?:live|LL)\b)` becomes 'maximum', and 'maximum (service )?LL' becomes 'maximum $1live load'. The frozen finder then routes to the existing chain: ANSWER L = (phi Pn - 1.2 D)/1.6 (tsel-30/31/32: 125.76; tcap-21: 149.5; ccap-307: 170), her method. Also accept 'max\.?' in reader ASKDEFS max_load (513). (2) No form solves for max DEAD, max TOTAL / D + L, or a load given as a ratio: STOP with one sentence and no number ('this page solves only for the maximum service LIVE load with D given; NOT answered here'), through amendRoute (route not_in_tool) or a stage refuse. tsel-33/34/35 STOP. (3) Depends on load-number-misbound (c), so that 'if D = 100k' / ', dead load = 100' no longer becomes L in step 1. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'maximum factored load the member can carry' and 'how much load can it carry' (capacity, STRENGTH_ASK), beam_max_live_load questions, 'Lmax', 'max spacing', the OA-28 / XA-29 / DS-28 variants that already work.

clusters.title: findBracing reads one brace with no axis, no negation, one height, and '1/3 points' as mid height, and fillColumn always puts it on the weak axis
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findBracing lines 1844-1856. (a) Line 1846 (and the fallback at 1852) matches 'braced/bracing ... mid height' with no look at the words before ('not braced', 'un-') or after ('is removed'), so a negated brace sets fraction = 2 (ccap-272/207, csel-03). (b) No axis words are read: 'about its strong axis', 'about the x axis', 'in the plane of the web', 'strong axis only'. fillColumn 1943-1952 then always sets Ly = L/n and Lx = L. Only bothDir (1943) moves it to Lx (ccap-187/271/178, csel-04: 460.2 for 208.8). (c) Line 1849 `w = /third/ ? 3 : /quarter/ ? 4 : 2` turns '1/3 points' into mid height (ccap-309). (d) Only the first brace statement is read, so 'weak axis at third points and strong axis at mid height' loses the second (ccap-281). (e) Line 1853 exec()s the 'N ft above/from the base' regex once, so '10 ft and 20 ft from the base' keeps only 20 (ccap-280, csel-19). The useSeg split is then 20/10.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js findBracing + fillColumn 1943-1956. (a) Negation: 'not|no|never|without' within the clause before the match, a 'un-' prefix, or '(is|are|was|been) (removed|omitted|taken out|eliminated)' after it means NO brace: ANSWER with L about both axes (unambiguous: ccap-272/207 466, csel-03 W12X65). A text with both a negated and a positive brace raises an ASK (need). (b) Axis: read the axis words in the brace's own clause. strong|major|x[- ]?axis|x-x|'in the plane of the web' gives 'x', so Lx = L/n and Ly = L (ANSWER 208.8 / 437.4, W14X90). weak|minor|y|'weak direction' or no axis word keeps the current Ly = L/n. 'both' keeps bothDir. Unclear words ('strong direction', 'perpendicular to the web') raise an ASK. (c) '1\/3' gives third and '1\/4' gives quarter (ANSWER 716). (d) Loop over every brace statement: two statements naming different axes set each axis (ccap-281: Ly = L/3, Lx = L/2: 764.0). Two statements for the same axis, or one that cannot be placed, raise an ASK. (e) Collect every 'N ft (and M ft) from/above the base|bottom'. Two or more heights on a pinned-pinned column give segments at those heights (brace = pin, her method; ANSWER 744.7 / W14X99). With a fixed end, use cluster column-segments-and-per-axis-K. Unclear raises an ASK.
